we have successfully extracted sources in our deepest 4.5 and 3.6 μm data at densities as high as about 100,000 per square degree, and that the flux density limits for the main field are 20, 20, 100, 100 μJansky at 3.6 4.5 5.8 and 8.μm, respectively.
the IRAC instrument has performed as expected and the data are suitable for a wide variety of scientific investigations.

(1) the IRAC data have been processed to produce high-quality, high-precision mosaics and reliable source catalogs, and that (2) the source density in these data is high enough to allow us to study the properties of the extragalactic sky in unprecedented detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the formation and evolution of galaxies and large-scale structures in the universe.

the study of infrared galaxies, and the IRAC data are the first step in a comprehensive study that will include data from the Multiband Imaging Photometer, the Infrared Spectrograph, and other telescopes.
the study of the infrared properties of extragalactic sources, including the identification of new infrared sources, their classification, and their physical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Spitzer IRAC instrument has met and exceeded its performance expectations.
we have successfully produced a set of catalogs and mosaics that are 99% reliable, and 80% complete at the stated flux density limits.
the IRAC Extragalactic Survey has been a resounding success.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully completed a survey of the extragalactic sky in the IRAC bands with a depth of ~1-2 orders of magnitude greater than any previous survey.

we have successfully demonstrated the ability of the IRAC instrument to perform extragalactic surveys at flux densities as low as 10 μJyr-1, and we have produced a large set of data that will be useful to a broad community of astronomers.
we have successfully demonstrated the ability of the Infrared Array Camera to detect and characterize the properties of faint sources in extragalactic surveys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IRAC instrument is capable of performing deep extragalactic surveys at all four of its wavelengths.
we have demonstrated the ability of IRAC to detect and measure the flux densities of faint sources at the required accuracy to enable a variety of science projects.
the IRAC data are of extremely high quality and that the instrument and data reduction pipeline are performing very well.
